title: U.S. House · Minnesota's 2nd District
area: South metro Twin Cities suburbs and exurbs, including Lakeville, Prior Lake, Burnsville, Eagan and Hastings.

context.text: This is an open seat: incumbent Rep. Angie Craig (D) did not run for re-election here, running instead in the Democratic primary for U.S. Senate (where she lost to Peggy Flanagan). Matt Little, a former state senator, won the Democratic primary over four others. Eric Pratt, a state senator, won the Republican primary unopposed on the ballot.

candidates.name: Matt Little

summary.text: Matt Little is the Democratic nominee for the open MN-02 seat. He is a former Minnesota state senator who grew up in the district, in Lakeville, and now lives in New Market Township.

background.text: Grew up in Lakeville, Minnesota (within the district), and attended high school in Rosemount; now lives in New Market Township.
Served in the Minnesota State Senate representing District 58 from 2017 to 2021, before losing re-election in 2020 to Zach Duckworth (R).

priorities.text: Says he is running to fight for people who work hard but 'still can't get ahead,' and for families struggling to afford groceries, child care, health care and assisted living.
Says he supports cutting red tape and eliminating wasteful spending, but opposes what he describes as cuts made by the current administration to life-saving programs.
Frames his campaign around defending democracy and the rule of law, and says he wants to work across the aisle with bipartisan experience.

positions.summary: Says he is fighting for families who cannot afford health care, and opposes federal cuts to vital public services.

record.text: Served as a Minnesota state senator representing District 58 from 2017 to 2021.

candidates.researchNotes: Matt Little has not completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey; positions are drawn from Ballotpedia's summary of his campaign website's 'Key Issues' page rather than a direct fetch of that page.

candidates.name: Eric Pratt
candidates.currentRole: Minnesota State Senator, District 54 (since 2021; previously District 35, 2013-2021)

summary.text: Eric Pratt is the Republican nominee for the open MN-02 seat. He is a sitting Minnesota state senator and former banking executive from Prior Lake.

background.text: Born and raised in Prior Lake, Minnesota; graduated from Prior Lake High School.
Earned a B.A. in economics from the University of Colorado, Boulder, where he played Division I football, and an M.B.A. in finance from the University of St. Thomas.
Worked in banking and finance, including roles as senior group manager at Target and senior vice president of risk management at U.S. Bank.
Began his public service on the Prior Lake-Savage school board before being elected to the Minnesota Senate in 2012.

priorities.text: 'Restore economic stability and opportunity': says he will focus on lowering costs and supporting small businesses.
'Protect communities and keep families safe': supports law enforcement and first responders, and says laws should be enforced consistently, including at the border.
'Keep bad actors out of our wallets': says he will work to crack down on fraud and abuse of government programs.

positions.summary: Says laws should be enforced fairly and consistently 'from our neighborhoods to the U.S. Border.'
Says he supports law enforcement, first responders and policies that keep communities secure.
Described himself as 'pro-life' in a 2012 campaign survey for state legislature; no more recent statement on abortion was found on his 2026 congressional campaign materials.

record.text: Has served in the Minnesota State Senate since 2013 (District 35, 2013-2021; District 54, 2021-present); currently ranking minority member of the Senate Finance Committee and a member of the Capital Investment and Jobs and Economic Growth Finance and Policy committees.
